name: Line REPL (ahohs chat)
description: Prompts, reads a line, runs it through the front door and draws the interim updates, the answer, the summary of the work and any question as plain text. Commands: /help, /trail, /later, /quit.
advantages: Standard library only and works over any pipe, so a script can drive it.
disadvantages: Each line is its own run because the front door takes no history, and the screen cannot replace a line in place.

name: Live session (reference terminal)
description: Runs any harness in a thread and draws its events in place on a terminal (plain lines elsewhere): current steps, a sub-agent tree, messages sent and taken up, a risky step waiting for y or n, elapsed time and cost; Escape or Ctrl-C stops and keeps the session, resume continues it, and the closing report lists what changed, what is left and the command that resumes. The structure tree (Tab, arrows) and the authority in force open only on request; the header shows spend and time against the ceilings; the soft limit and the hub's stop decision are one line each; a typed line after a run continues the session and `/harness` switches harness between runs (`WorkTerminal`, `ahohs work`).
advantages: Stdlib only; one driver for the hub loop, a stream session or any Harness; every control is shown as taken or not available; the same events replay to the same screen.
disadvantages: Redraw assumes an ANSI terminal; a line editor is minimal (no history, no multi-line); stopping the hub loop waits for the model call in flight.
